messages.subject: Deducer question...
messages.body_plain:
I start Deducer from an existing R session using the JGR() function.
When I do this, it starts a new R console (seems like a new instance
of R) along with the Deducer GUI. This new instance of R does not have
access to all the objects that I had created in the existing R
session. Is there a way to keep these two R sessions synchronized?
Can the two sessions be linked somehow?

messages.subject: Can "Reshape2" package by Hadley Wickham RESHAPE Deducer?
messages.subject_clean: Can "Reshape2" package by Hadley Wickham RESHAPE Deducer?
messages.body_plain:
I don't know if anybody else have had the same idea or wish that "reshape2" package can see the light in Deducer with its no-doubt impressive features of melting and casting the data into any shape the user wants. These two features will circumvent the need of many functions scattered amond different packages and not easily available at disposal in ONE-CONTEXT FRAMA (i.e. reshape2 package) esp. that this package has been written by ggplot2 founder Hadley Wickham. Do we have here an important data management boost to Deducer which is already an ever-green user-friendly tool?

thanks alot

messages.subject_clean: Is it possible to work with projected data in DeducerSpatial
messages.body_plain:
I am working with SpatialDeducer and I was able to load a projected shapefile by changing the "proj" argument.

Is it possible to copy and paste the parameters for the desired projection instead of writing it every time?

Also, how do I convert a data.frame that has the latitude and longitude projected (not decimal degrees)?

When I try to load a txt file with UTM values, I get the following error:

> sitiosCRTM05qgis_temp <- sitiosCRTM05qgis
> if (class(sitiosCRTM05qgis[, 'x']) == 'factor') {
+ sitiosCRTM05qgis_temp[,'x'] <- as.numeric(as.character(sitiosCRTM05qgis_temp[, 'x']))
+ }
> if (class(sitiosCRTM05qgis[, 'y']) == 'factor') {
+ sitiosCRTM05qgis_temp[,'y'] <- as.numeric(as.character(sitiosCRTM05qgis_temp[, 'y']))
+ }
> sitiosCRTM05qgis_temp <- subset(sitiosCRTM05qgis_temp,
+ !is.na <http://is.na>(x)  & !is.na <http://is.na>(y) )
> puntos <- SpatialPointsDataFrame(sitiosCRTM05qgis_temp[,c('x', 'y')], data=sitiosCRTM05qgis_temp,proj4string=CRS('+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84'))
Error en validityMethod(as(object, superClass)) :
  Geographical CRS given to non-conformant data:  500632.8451 1192979.4670
> puntos <- spTransform(puntos,osm())
Error en spTransform(puntos, osm()) :
  error in evaluating the argument 'x' in selecting a method for function 'spTransform': Error: objeto 'puntos' no encontrado
> rm(sitiosCRTM05qgis_temp)

Best,

Manuel

Best,

Manuel

messages.subject: Re: GLM (Generalized linear model) for stat_smooth
messages.body_plain:
Hi Manuel:
I found the example below by typing ?stat_smooth

qplot(Age, as.numeric(Kyphosis) - 1, data = kyphosis) +
  stat_smooth(method="glm", family="binomial")
qplot(Age, as.numeric(Kyphosis) - 1, data=kyphosis) +
  stat_smooth(method="glm", family="binomial", formula = y ~ ns(x, 2))

messages.subject: Deducer on Xubuntu 12.04
messages.body_plain:
I'm having difficulties installing Deducer on a fresh installation of Xubuntu...latest release (12.04). Anyone else use this distribution or any other Ubuntu flavor of the latest release?

I get the following configuration errors.

configure: error: One or more Java configuration variables are not set.
Make sure R is configured with full Java support (including JDK). Run
R CMD javareconf
as root to add Java support to R.

If you don't have root privileges, run
R CMD javareconf -e
to set all Java-related variables and then install rJava.

Following these instructions doesn't seem to matter.

Thanks! Deducer is fantastic and I'll change distros to use it if I have to!

BC

messages.subject: Re: Adding ListDataListener to VariableListWidget
messages.body_plain:
Hi Bill,

I'm a little late with the reply, but I've fixed this, and it will be
in the next version of Deducer. Due out on aug 27th.

ian

On Fri, Jul 13, 2012 at 8:03 AM, Bill <alter...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I'm working on a package that includes a preview screen and I would like the
> preview to refresh each time there is a change in the variables in a
> VariableListWidget (that's the widget that the variables move INTO).  I'm
> working in Java because there is no preview widget yet.  All the selections
> that would trigger the change are in a SimpleRSubdialog called "Options".
> Here's the beginning:
>
> public class WideToLong2 extends RDialog implements KeyListener,
> ActionListener, ListSelectionListener, ListDataListener {
> ...
> Options = new SimpleRSubDialog(this,"Options");
> ...
> optionDataSelector = new VariableSelectorWidget();
> ...
> DropVariables = new VariableListWidget("Variables to
> Drop",optionDataSelector);
>
> I would like to add a ListDataListener to DropVariables so that whenever the
> variables in that VariableListWidget change, the preview updates.  The
> addListener method for VariableListWidget has different effects depending on
> the type of EventListener that is assigned, but none of these are
> ListDataListeners:
>
>     public void addListener(EventListener lis) {
>         if(lis instanceof ActionListener){
>             removeButton.addActionListener((ActionListener) lis);
>             addButton.addActionListener((ActionListener) lis);
>         }
>         if(lis instanceof ListSelectionListener)
>             varList.addListSelectionListener((ListSelectionListener) lis);
>         if(lis instanceof MouseListener)
>             varList.addMouseListener((MouseListener) lis);
>
> I thought I could extract the model from DropVariables and then assign a
> listener to that.  The getModel method for VariableListWidget is:
>
> public Object getModel() {
>         return varList.getModel();
>     }
>
> where varList is defined as a DJList, which extends JList and has
> DefaultListModel as its model.  To get to it:
>
> DefaultListModel dropModel = (DefaultListModel)DropVariables.getModel();
> dropModel.addListDataListener(new LDListener());
>
> where LDListener is a class implementing ListDataListener.
>
> Unfortunately, that doesn't work.  Attaching a listener to the add or remove
> buttons doesn't work either, because the listener fires before those buttons
> have their effects on changing the model.  Does anyone have suggestions on
> how to listen for changes to the DefaultListModel model of a
> VariableListWidget?
>
> Thanks,
> --Bill
messages.body_snippet:
Hi Bill,

I'm a little late with the reply, but I've fixed this, and it will be
in the next version of Deducer. Due out on aug 27th.

ian

messages.subject: Installation issue
messages.body_plain:
First, it doesn't sound like you are using  Linux as the message subject implied. What operating system are you on?

Second, do you have java installed on your machine? If not install it.

Third, you will want to run jgr through the launcher.

Follow the instructions on deducer.org <http://deducer.org>

Best
Ian

Sent from my iPhone
